question.value: What is the radio emission mechanism of the circumplanetary environment around PDS 70c, and why is PDS 70c detected in the sub-millimetre continuum while PDS 70b is not?

evidence.quote: Knowledge of the emission mechanisms may enable observations of accretion rates and physical conditions in the circumplanetary environment.
The sub-millimetre detection of PDS 70c thus raises the questions of what the nature of the emission is, and why PDS 70c is detected in the sub-millimetre continuum, while PDS 70b is not.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit parametric CPD SED models (dusty disc, jet, H I free-free, uniform slab, and magnetic disc with metals and H-)

method.value: Construct analytic and semi-analytic SED models for a dusty viscous CPD, a dusty CPD plus optically thin/thick ionised jet, a viscous CPD with H I free-free emission, a uniform pill-box slab, and a magnetised CPD with metal and H- free-free and bound-free opacities; sample posterior parameter distributions against the coeval Bands 3, 4, 7, and 9 SED using Nautilus.

evidence.quote: The posterior distributions on the free parameters of our SED models were sampled with the `Nautilus` package (cite: Lange2023MNRAS.525.3181L), which implements nested sampling aided by neuronal networks.

We considered four models for the observed SED. Firstly, we considered only the dust component from the CPD. Secondly, we included an optically thin jet. Thirdly, we included an optically thick jet. Finally, we included free-free emission from the disc itself, using an $\alpha$-constant disc and a magnetic disc. We also guided our analysis using a uniform slab model, adding the contribution of free electrons from metals in the magnetic disc.

key_parameters.value: M_p = 4 M_Jup, d = 112.3 pc, orbital radius = 34 au, R_out = 1/3 R_Hill ~ 1.23 au, R_p = R_in = 1 R_Jup, kappa_R = 10 cm^2/g, T_floor = 27 K, mu = 1

evidence.quote: We opted for a planetary mass of $M_{\rm p}=4 \, M_{\rm Jup}$, given the upper limit of $4.9 \, M_{\rm Jup}$ (cite: Doi2024ApJ...974L..25D) and the restriction of $4 \, M_{\rm Jup}<M_{\rm p}< 12 \, M_{\rm Jup}$ (cite: Haffert2019NatAs...3..749H).

PDS 70 is at a distance of $112.3 \, {\rm pc}$ (cite: Gaia2023A&A...674A...1G), and we adopted a planetary orbital radius for PDS 70c of $34 \, {\rm au}$ (cite: Haffert2019NatAs...3..749H), implying an outer CPD radius of $R_{\rm out}=1/3\,\ensuremath{{R_{\textnormal{Hill}}}}\sim 1.23 \, {\rm au}$ (cite: Quillen1998ApJ...508..707Q)

We used $T_{\rm floor}=27 \, {\rm K}$, which was obtained by extrapolating the dust physical conditions in the outer ring obtained by multi-frequency SED fits (these dust diagnostics will be documented in a forthcoming article).

key_parameters.value: Jet spectral index alpha_jet = 0.4 (optically thick) or -0.1 (optically thin); magnetic disc alpha(R) > 10^-5

evidence.quote: If the jet is partially optically thick, an upper limit is set on the spectral index with $\alpha_{\rm jet}=0.4$ (cite: Carrasco2016ApJ...821L..16C). In the case of an optically thin jet, $\alpha_{\rm jet}=-0.1$.
We therefore imposed a lower limit, $\alpha(R) > 10^{-5}$.

assumptions.value: Dust opacity kappa_mm = 3.4 * zeta * (0.87 mm / lambda) cm^2/g; hydrostatic Gaussian vertical gas profile; LTE ionisation via Saha equation; solar photospheric abundances for H, He, Na, Mg, K without dust depletion; n_i = n_H- = n_e = 0 when H- >= 10% of ions

evidence.quote: The dust opacity is $\kappa_{\rm mm}=3.4 \zeta \times \frac{0.87 \rm mm}{\lambda} \, {\rm cm}^{2}/ {\rm g}$ (cite: Andrews2012ApJ...744..162A), and the optical depth $\tau_{\rm mm}=\kappa_{\rm mm} \Sigma / 2$.
We assumed that the metals are not depleted into dust.

In the case in which the number density of ${\rm H}^{-}$ becomes significant (10% of the ions or more), the free electrons are less abundant in the medium. The number density of free electrons decreases drastically and we set $n_{\rm i}=n_{{\rm H}^{-}}=n_{{\rm e}}=0$.

claims.hypothesis: The radio SED of PDS 70c arises from thermal dust emission in a viscous circumplanetary disc (with or without an ionised jet).
claims.experiment: Measured the coeval multi-frequency ALMA SED of PDS 70c in Bands 3, 4, 7, and 9 and fitted parametric dusty viscous CPD models (with and without optically thin/thick jets) using Nautilus.
claims.result: The observed SED has alpha = 2.0 +/- 0.2 from Band 3 to Band 7 and drops below an optically thick extrapolation in Band 9 at 2.6 sigma, whereas dusty disc models with realistic floor temperatures (T_floor = 27 K) produce steeper spectral indices (alpha > 2.35) and overshoot Band 9; inferred dust-to-gas ratio upper limits are < 10^-4.80.
claims.finding: A purely dusty viscous disc (even with ionised jets) is inconsistent with the data, and PDS 70c is depleted of sub-millimetre-emitting dust by a factor of at least 1000.

evidence.quote: A viscous dusty disc is inconsistent with the data, even with the inclusion of ionised jets.
The best fits obtained for the dusty disc model, shown in Fig.6, have spectral indices of $\alpha >2.35$ and do not fit the data, even between Bands 3 and 7.
Given an optically thick free-free spectrum, any steeper component is negligible, and the dust-to-gas mass ratio $\zeta$ must be very low, $\log(\zeta)<-4.80$.

claims.hypothesis: The Band 9 non-detection of PDS 70c is caused by sub-millimetre flux variability between observation epochs.
claims.experiment: Analysed nine Band 7 execution blocks spanning seven epochs from May to November 2023 by subtracting the circumstellar disc in the uv plane and fitting the point-source flux density of PDS 70c at each epoch.
claims.result: The weighted average Band 7 flux density is 130 +/- 4 uJy with a weighted scatter of 9.3% across all seven epochs, and multi-frequency measurements are coeval within two months.
claims.finding: The radio emission of PDS 70c is constant within ~10% in 2023, making it unlikely that variability caused the Band 9 non-detection.

evidence.quote: The weighted average is $130\pm 4~\mu$Jy, with a weighted scatter of 9.3%. Therefore the flux density of PDS 70c is constant across all seven epochs within $\sim$10%.
It seems unlikely that this non-detection is caused by variability, given Sec. 2.4, and since PDS 70c is readily detected in Bands 4 and 7 at $\sim 5\,\sigma$ and $\sim 9\,\sigma$ respectively.

claims.hypothesis: Atomic plasma radiation (metal and H- free-free) from a magnetised CPD or H I free-free from a viscous H II CPD can account for the full radio SED of PDS 70c including the Band 9 turnover.
claims.experiment: Extended parametric viscous and magnetic CPD models to compute LTE ionisation of H, He, Na, Mg, K, and H-, and fitted the emergent free-free and bound-free SEDs to the ALMA data.
claims.result: Viscous H II disc models yield huge emission measures (EM ~ 10^26-31 cm^-6 pc) and overshoot Band 9 (F_671 = 389–417 uJy); magnetic disc models reach moderate emission measures (EM ~ 10^11.5 cm^-6 pc) and metal free-free turns thin above ~500 GHz, but H- free-free opacity keeps tau ~ 1 and overshoots Band 9 (F_671 = 339 uJy).
claims.finding: Both H II viscous disc and magnetised atomic plasma disc models marginally account for the optically thick spectrum up to Band 7 (within 3 sigma of Band 9), but fail to reproduce the optically thin turnover at Band 9.

evidence.quote: However, the $\ensuremath{\rm H ^{-}}$ opacity still results in an optically thick SED, overshooting Band 9.

Now we could produce spectral indices of $(\alpha_{97.5}^{145},\alpha_{145}^{343.5}, \alpha_{343.5}^{671}) = (1.85, 1.71, 1.72)$ that could marginally fit the data, and overestimate Band 9 with a flux $F_{671}$ of 339 $\mu {\rm Jy}$.
However, the optical depth of ${\rm H}^{-}$ begins to dominate above 500 GHz, and the total optical depth remains $\tau \sim 1$ without reaching the optically thin regime.

claims.hypothesis: The radio SED of PDS 70c, including the optically thin turnover in Band 9, originates from H I free-free emission in an accretion shock at the surface of the CPD rather than a planetary photospheric shock or accretion funnels.
claims.experiment: Fitted uniform slab models to determine required emitting sizes and temperatures, tested a photospheric shock size of R_max = 2 R_Jup, and ran 1D shock-heated gas simulations following Aoyama et al. (2018) for pre-shock velocities of 30 and 50 km/s.
claims.result: A 2 R_Jup emitting region requires log(T/K) = 6.83 (+0.04/-0.10), which is unphysical for planetary shocks; a 7000–10^4 K slab requires R_max ~ 52–62 R_Jup (~0.025–0.078 au) and EM ~ 10^11–10^12 cm^-6 pc, and CPD surface shock simulations produce tau > 1 at 300 GHz turning over to tau ~ a few times 0.1 at 600 GHz.
claims.finding: Photospheric shocks and accretion funnels are ruled out, whereas H I free-free emission from a thin shocked layer at the CPD surface reproduces both the optically thick lower-frequency SED and the Band 9 turnover.

evidence.quote: We find that the optically thin turnover at $\gtrsim$$600$ GHz is only recovered if a thin shocked layer is present at the CPD surface, as is suggested by simulations. A photospheric shock or accretion funnels are ruled out as radio emission sources because their small solid angles require $T\sim$$10^{6}$ K, which are unrealistic temperatures in planetary shock accretion.

In both cases, the emission at 300 GHz is optically thick ($\tau>1$) but turns over into an optically thin spectrum at 600 GHz ($\tau \sim$ a few times $0.1$). This is also the case for the SED of PDS 70c obtained with the uniform slab model, with a best fit of $\tau_{300\,\rm GHz}\approx 3$ and $\tau_{600 \rm GHz}\approx 0.6$.

why_this_data.value: Multi-frequency ALMA observations across Bands 3, 4, 7, and 9 acquired within ~two months avoid variability bias and span the frequency range needed to distinguish thermal dust (alpha ~ 3) from free-free emission (alpha <= 2) and test predictions of bright Band 9 CPD dust emission.

Measurements involving Bands 3, 4, 7, and 9 in 2023 are spread over two months (except for the November 2023 execution blocks in Band 7 and the December 2023 TM2 execution block in Band 9), and are the least biased by variability compared to the 2017 and 2019 data.

limitations_admitted.value: The jet flux formula was developed for stellar jets and is extrapolated into the planetary mass regime.

evidence.quote: It should be borne in mind that these formulae were developed for stellar jets, rather than protoplanets, and that they are being extrapolated into the planetary mass regime.

limitations_admitted.value: Magnetic disc viscosity estimates neglect external ionisation sources (interstellar UV and cosmic rays) at large radii.

limitations_admitted.value: The atomic plasma model depends heavily on extrapolating H- free-free opacities from Gray (2022) (valid up to 10 um and T = 2500–10000 K) to millimetre wavelengths and cooler temperatures (T ~ 1000–2000 K).

evidence.quote: (cite: Gray2022oasp.book.....G) was inspired by works that calculated opacities of up to $10\,\mu$m and in a range of temperatures from 2500 to 10000 K. This is very important here, since we are calculating the opacity at millimetre wavelengths, and in a cold disc where the majority of the flux comes from temperatures of $T\approx1000$–2000 K.

limitations_admitted.value: Achieving a pre-shock free-fall velocity > 30 km/s at 62 R_Jup requires a minimum planetary mass of 15.7 M_Jup (above the 2 sigma dynamical upper limit of 13.6 M_Jup) and spatially constant mass flux models yield very high mass influx rates, as radially varying v_0 and mass flux were not modelled.

evidence.quote: A minimum planetary mass of 15.7 $M_{\rm Jup}$ is required, which is 2.1 $M_{\rm Jup}$ above the $2\sigma$ upper limit of 13.6 $M_{\rm Jup}$ estimated for the dynamical mass of PDS 70c (cite: Trevascus2025A&A...698A..19T). This minimum planetary mass could be reduced by considering the increasing $\varv_0$ at smaller radii, and its resulting radio flux, but this is beyond the scope of this work.

referee_caveats_inferred: The Band 9 turnover relies on a 2.6 sigma discrepancy from an optically thick extrapolation in a dataset where TM1 suffered weather-related low-spatial-frequency phase noise (requiring uv-clipping < 0.4 Mlambda and a 1/0.78 cross-calibration scaling with TM2).
The Band 7 flux density of PDS 70c differs between the restored map peak (111 +/- 14 uJy) and the deconvolved gpuvmem Gaussian fit (157 +/- 27 uJy) due to confusion with the cavity wall.

The favoured CPD surface shock scenario with spatially uniform pre-shock velocity requires a planetary mass (15.7 M_Jup) exceeding dynamical upper limits unless radially dependent infall velocities and concentrated mass loading are invoked.

Further develops the imaging and VisAlign alignment strategy used across epochs and configurations
Provides the baseline parametric viscous dusty circumplanetary disc model extended in this work
Provides the parametric magnetised CPD model and magnetospheric accretion framework
Provides the post-shock gas model used to simulate free-free emission from a CPD surface shock
Introduces the Nautilus neural-network-assisted nested sampling package used for SED parameter inference
